text:
Alex: seeing a bunch of GPU attach failures in us-west1 this morning, approx 15% of provisioning attempts fail with timeout. digging into node logs now.
Maya: ugh, same. noticed a spike in nvme util and queued requests around 02:12 UTC.
Alex: posting iostat snapshot from one of the failed hosts:
```
avg-cpu:  %user   %nice %system %iowait  %steal   %idle
          4.1    0.0    2.6   78.4    0.0   15.0
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         120.2  430.5  5120.0  98000.0  45.3   4.2  98.7
```
Alex: nvme %util ~99%, write queueing high. traces show many small writes from the ephemeral janitor scrub.
janitor-bot: janitor: starting scrub cycle on scratchpool at 02:10 UTC, concurrency=24, target_batch=256
Maya: looks like the cleanup job ran at the same time as the nightly batch-alloc window (02:00-03:00). bad timing.
Sam: that concurrency is too aggressive for us-west1 hardware profile. scrub causes write amplification + high small-io pressure.
Priya: can we throttle janitor or reduce concurrency as hotfix? We need quick mitigation to restore GPU attach success.
Sam: short term: reduce janitor concurrency from 24 -> 4 and reduce target_batch to 64. add ionice/blkio throttling to systemd unit. example snippet:
```
[Service]
CPUShares=512
IOSchedulingClass=2
IOSchedulingPriority=7
BlockIODeviceWeight=200
```
Sam: that should drop io pressure without pausing cleanup entirely.
Maya: agree. also we can add a guard in the janitor to backoff if nvme util > 80% or if gpu-provision-failures metric spikes.
Alex: can we deploy the concurrency change now? who owns janitor?
Sam: I do, i'll push a patch to lower concurrency and add the io config. will test on staging then roll to us-west1-canary host group.
Priya: operationally, we should also tweak autoscaler to avoid scheduling big batch allocs during scrub windows. longer term: move heavy scrubs to cold hours per-region.
Maya: also consider switching scratchpool default to use write-optimized partitions for batch nodes, or add small local buffer SSD pool for transient write bursts. cost tradeoff though.
Alex: cost question: if we add a higher endurance tier for scratch in us-west1, what's the delta? finance_estimate: roughly +$0.12/hr per host. need approval if we scale fleet.
Priya: for now keep it cheap and do throttling/backoff. Sam, can you include a quick metric alert that fires if nvme util >85% for 2m?
Sam: yes, adding alert and a janitor backoff hook.
janitor-bot: janitor: patch queued by Sam -> scrub concurrency change proposed.
Maya: thanks. once canary looks good, open a short runbook note so oncall knows how to revert or pause janitor quickly.
Alex: ack. assigning Sam for fix, Priya to own alert, Maya to write short runbook. I'll follow-up in infra postmortem next week. :thumbsup:
Priya: quick question — do we have telemetry per-block-device by pod? would help to pinpoint noisy tenants.
Sam: not currently per-pod, only per-node. plan: add cgroup-level io stats to the observability backlog. low-priority but valuable.
Maya: we'll move the scrub schedule to 05:00 UTC for us-west1 for next week as a precaution.
Alex: closing thread for now, monitoring. will reopen if GPU attach failures continue. :eyes:
